title: No Escape: Refugees Face a Climate Crisis They Did Least to Cause
title_zh: 无处可逃：难民正面对他们最无辜的气候危机
source_name: UN News — “‘No Escape’ for refugees on the frontlines of the climate crisis” (6 Nov 2026); UNHCR No Escape III report
summary_zh: 联合国难民署 11 月 6 日在《无处可逃》第三期报告中警告：全球约四分之三、近 9000 万被迫流离失所者生活在干旱、洪水与极端高温等高风险国家。脆弱与受冲突影响的收容国只拿到全球气候资金约一成。报告称气候冲击正在摧毁住所、削弱生计，也让安全返乡更难；同时难民与收容社区已在萨赫勒太阳能供水、乌干达气候韧性农业、哥伦比亚红树林修复等方面探索解决办法。COP31 将于下周在土耳其安塔利亚开幕。
paragraphs: Nearly three in four forcibly displaced people — almost 90 million — now live in countries with high to severe exposure to drought, floods and extreme heat, the UN refugee agency warned on 6 November. The finding comes from UNHCR's latest report, No Escape III, published ahead of the COP31 climate conference next week in Antalya, Türkiye.

"Refugees face a double injustice," said Antón Leis García, Assistant High Commissioner for Operations. Forced to flee conflicts they did not cause, they are now on the frontlines of a climate crisis they have contributed least to. For millions, climate change is not a distant threat: it is destroying shelters, undermining livelihoods and putting hopes of rebuilding at risk.

Fragile and conflict-affected countries that host large refugee populations receive only around 10 per cent of global climate finance. The report follows people such as Monira Bahraldin, who fled war in Sudan's Darfur region and now lives in a settlement in eastern Chad. There, drought and conflict make the dry season hotter, and the journey to fetch water grows longer even as families need more of it.

Heat and floods are set to worsen. By 2050, one in three refugee settlements across sub-Saharan Africa could face at least 100 days of dangerous heat each year. Severe flooding linked to El Niño may force three million people across Somalia, Kenya, South Sudan and Uganda to leave their homes by the end of 2026. Weather-related disasters have triggered hundreds of millions of internal displacements over the past decade.

Climate risks also weaken lasting solutions. More than two-thirds of refugees who returned home in the first half of 2026 went back to countries highly vulnerable to climate hazards. In Syria, nearly four million people have recently returned, yet declining groundwater and shocks such as Euphrates River flooding in May damaged homes and displaced thousands once again. Nearly 90 per cent of the world's stateless people live in highly exposed countries and often struggle to reach relief because they lack legal recognition.

The report also highlights hope. Refugees and host communities are developing solar-powered water systems in the Sahel, climate-resilient agriculture in Uganda and mangrove restoration in Colombia. "Refugees are on the frontlines of the climate crisis, but they are also part of the solution," Mr. Leis García said. He urged COP31 to recognise their leadership and turn commitments into concrete investments that reach those most at risk.
paragraphs_zh: 联合国难民署 11 月 6 日警告：全球近四分之三、约 9000 万被迫流离失所者，如今生活在干旱、洪水和极端高温等高至严重风险的国家。这一结论来自难民署最新报告《无处可逃》第三期，发布时机正值下周将在土耳其安塔利亚举行的 COP31 气候大会之前。
负责行动事务的助理高级专员安东·莱斯·加西亚说：“难民面临双重不公。”他们被迫逃离并非由自己造成的冲突，如今又站在自己贡献最少的气候危机的前线。对数百万人而言，气候变化不是遥远威胁：它正在摧毁住所、削弱生计，并使重建生活的希望岌岌可危。
收容大量难民的脆弱与受冲突影响国家，只获得全球气候资金约 10%。报告跟踪了像莫尼拉·巴拉尔丁这样的人：她逃离苏丹达尔富尔地区的战争，如今住在乍得东部的一处定居点。那里干旱与冲突并存，旱季更热，取水路程更长，而家庭对水的需求却在增加。
高温与洪水预计会加剧。到 2050 年，撒哈拉以南非洲三分之一的难民定居点，每年可能面临至少 100 天的危险高温。与厄尔尼诺相关的严重洪水，到 2026 年底可能迫使索马里、肯尼亚、南苏丹和乌干达约 300 万人离开家园。过去十年，与天气相关的灾害已在全球引发数以亿计的境内流离失所。
气候风险也削弱了持久解决办法。2026 年上半年返乡的难民中，超过三分之二回到了高度易受气候危害影响的国家。在叙利亚，近 400 万人近来已返乡，但地下水下降，以及 5 月幼发拉底河洪水等冲击，又损毁房屋并再次使数千人流离失所。全球近 90% 的无国籍者生活在高度暴露于气候风险的国家，往往因缺乏法律身份而难以获得救济。
报告也指出希望。难民与收容社区正在发展萨赫勒地区的太阳能供水系统、乌干达的气候韧性农业，以及哥伦比亚的红树林修复。莱斯·加西亚说：“难民站在气候危机的前线，但他们也是解决方案的一部分。”他敦促 COP31 承认他们的领导力，并把承诺转化为能到达最脆弱人群的具体投资。

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
options: COP31 has already solved climate risks for all refugees.
Most refugees live far from climate hazards and need less funding.
Many refugees live in climate-risk countries, receive too little climate finance, and need recognition plus real investment — while also helping invent solutions.
Stateless people are never affected by floods or heat.
questions.explanation: 主旨：大量难民生活在气候高风险国家，气候资金严重不足；报告呼吁承认其领导力并落实投资，同时也展示难民与收容社区正在参与解决办法。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the Syria example about return after conflict?
options: Returning home always ends displacement permanently.
Climate shocks can push returned people into displacement again even after war-related return.
Groundwater problems only affect countries without refugees.
Flooding along the Euphrates never damages homes.
